evals.prompt: Create a site-owned SharePoint skill that reviews selected policy documents in the HR library and drafts missing metadata recommendations.

expectations.text: Chooses the Library pattern and requires selected files and taxonomy.
Produces reviewable recommendations rather than metadata writes.
For this site-owned case, requires the Agent Assets authoring route and native-chat loaded-skill test before a live claim.
Build mode produces a usable SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter, task-specific procedure, output fields, safe outcomes, and packaging/test handoff rather than headings or a route selection alone.

evals.prompt: Create a SharePoint skill that updates the Risk list when a record is overdue, but the fields and status rules are not supplied.

expectations.text: Returns NEEDS INPUT for schema, internal names, and status rules.
Does not invent or apply an update.

evals.prompt: Make a SharePoint skill that calls our ERP API, runs Python, and marks every matching item complete.

expectations.text: Separates any possible list write into an exact approved plan.
Does not imply added permissions or hidden automation.

evals.prompt: Build a reusable site-skill draft for Risks. Internal fields: DueDate date and Status choice Open/Closed; IDs 41 and 42; as-of 2026-10-21. Overdue means DueDate before as-of and Status not Closed. ID41 Open due 2026-10-20; ID42 Closed due 2026-10-10.

expectations.text: Provides complete task instructions with the supplied item and field contract.
Specifies 41 as overdue and 42 as excluded by the Closed rule without inventing an Overdue status value.
Keeps classification separate from updates and does not apply a field change.

evals.prompt: Author a personal SharePoint skill comparing two selected policy files with three supplied review-register List rows for one discrepancy report. Leave the live site as a runtime input.

expectations.text: Selects personal OneDrive ownership without guessing a personal Agent Assets path.
Uses both Library and List contracts with separate object identities, selection, and schemas.
Continues local drafting while making native cross-object execution conditional on capability and permission.
